Lighting Controls in Storage Garages — partial. Applied: (1) zone area is CHECKED against the 360 m2 limit and an oversized zone is a shouted finding (re-zoning to satisfy a lighting rule would silently change the thermal results, so it is not done for you); (2) a >=30% unoccupied reduction is applied by schedule modulation — the 4.2.2.1.(16)-(23) convention, and note the general occupancy path CANNOT serve this since it is gated on LPD > 8.6 W/m2 while both garage records sit at 1.5-1.9 W/m2, and the Table 4.3.2.10 factors would give only 26.8%; (4) luminaire power within 6.1 m of a >=40% net-opening perimeter wall is derived as LPD x band area (the 4.2.2.1 convention) and a zone daylighting control is added above 150 W. Table 4.2.1.6. defers 'Storage garage interior' here rather than to 4.2.2.1.(10)/(13), so garages are correctly excluded from the ordinary photocontrol rule. Gaps: (3) covered vehicle ENTRANCES AND EXITS cannot be identified from geometry or space type — no model attribute distinguishes an entrance bay from a parking bay — so the 50% sunset-to-sunrise reduction is applied only when the modeller names those spaces, and is declared otherwise; its night window is a fixed schedule approximation rather than true astronomical sunset. (5) the daylight-transition-zone and ramp-without-parking exemptions are likewise not detectable, so the determinations are applied to every garage space and an exempt space must be excluded by the reviewer. (2)'s 20-minute detection delay is recorded in the audit but not modelled: an hourly ScheduleRuleset cannot express it

With a uniform space-level LPD that power is exactly LPD x daylighted_area. Exceptions honoured: (12)(a) obstruction ratio >=2 from ShadingSurfaces, (12)(b) glazing <2 m2, (12)(c) retail, (15)(b) skylight VT <0.4, (15)(c) >55 degN with <200 W.
